Maya Patel: Heads up — seeing 503s on hosted API, correlates with GPU pool us-west-2 queueing. Large spike in enqueue time and admission rejections. Anyone oncall?
Samir Rao: I'm looking. Metrics show pool `dedicated-gpu-us-west2` 100% utilization and queue depth skyrocketed ~18:12 UTC. Autoscaler didn't add capacity.
Li Chen: I can reproduce the queue backlog in the dashboard — prefix cache hit-rate is normal, so it's not KV cache. Looks like requests are piling up waiting for GPU slots.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2025-0427 created, severity=P1, oncall=@Samir Rao, pagerduty link <https://pd/redwood/INC-2025-0427>.
Samir Rao: Dumping admission controller log now, paste below:
```
admission_control.go: WARN reject request capacity exceeded pool=dedicated-gpu-us-west2 tokens=0 backlog=124 latency_ms=2034
autoscaler.go: INFO evaluate: desired=12 current=12 pending_scale=false reason="min_capacity_met"
resource_manager.go: ERROR heartbeat timeout to node-agent ip=10.3.22.19 err=rpc deadline exceeded
```
Nate Gomez: Autoscaler reported desired==current because it used a stale view of node resources — seeing a metrics ingestion lag for ~3m. Could be the metrics pipeline in that region.
Li Chen: Network flaps reported by cloud provider in us-west-2 around 18:09-18:14 UTC, partial connectivity loss to the telemetry cluster. That matches ingestion lag.
Maya Patel: So chain: network hiccup -> metrics lag -> autoscaler doesn't scale -> pool saturates -> admission control starts rejecting -> clients retry -> traffic amplifies -> other pools share token bucket and start throttling -> cascade.
Samir Rao: Mitigation: 18:16 increased pool size manually from 12->18 (temporary), 18:18 enabled circuit breaker to route low-priority traffic to cpu-fallback model, 18:22 rolled restart of node-agent on 3 flapping nodes. 503s dropped to baseline by 18:28.
Li Chen: Confirmed fallback reduced GPU load by ~27%. Clients saw elevated latency for ~10m but no more hard failures.
Nate Gomez: Root cause hypothesis: metrics ingestion outage made autoscaler read stale metrics and evaluate scale-down/hold incorrectly. Secondary contributing factor: admission controller uses a shared token bucket across multiple pools; when a single pool saturates, burst tokens were drained and caused broad throttling.
Maya Patel: Logs show admission controller rejects include this message: `shared_bucket.go: WARN tokens=0 drained_by=dedicated-gpu-us-west2`. That explains cascading effect.
Samir Rao: Action items proposed (brief):
- (Samir) Add fallbacks in autoscaler to use short-lived local estimates if metrics pipeline lag detected (ETA 2w).
- (Li) Split token buckets per-pool or add weighted isolation to prevent single pool draining global tokens (ETA 3w).
- (Nate) Add synthetic heartbeats for node-agent so autoscaler can detect partial telemetry loss vs actual capacity (ETA 1w).
- (Maya) Add runbook step for manually routing low-priority traffic to CPU-fallback and increasing pool size (ETA docs update 3d).
Maya Patel: Also adding a short-term tweak: if metrics ingestion lag > 60s, autoscaler should fall back to pod-level kube metrics (PR drafted).
ops-bot: Postmortem tag applied, adding owners: Samir, Li, Nate.
Li Chen: One more note — billing noticed a small spike due to manual scale-up; we should include cost guardrail in runbook so we don't exceed emergency budget without approval.
Samir Rao: Will include a cost check in the manual scale play.
Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. I'll schedule a 30m postmortem tomorrow 16:00 UTC to capture detailed timeline and finalize RCA. Please drop any logs or snippets here before EOD. :+1:
